mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% within 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over 3 months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to higher prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% within a month signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, but only during a late-cycle expansion regime.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met during a late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in GDP (GDPC1) and a decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% within 3 months signals a positive supply shock, which increases real output and reduces inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases & CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.
